title: Australia Council Bill 2013
portfolio: Regional Australia, Local Government, Arts and Sport

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would replace the Australia Council's governing framework, updating its arts support functions, decision-making structure, corporate planning requirements and reporting responsibilities.
It would introduce a board appointed for relevant skills and let the Council establish committees, including arrangements for assessing grant applications through peers.
The Council would continue as a statutory body, with the main provisions starting by proclamation or after a six-month fallback period following Royal Assent.
changes: The Council would gain express functions to conduct arts research and publish evaluations of its support.
The Council could provide financial assistance and guarantees in carrying out its functions.
Australian artists would be defined by citizenship or permanent residency for the legislation's purposes.
The Minister could direct some Council activities but could not direct decisions on financial assistance or guarantees.
summary.affected: Australian artists, arts organisations, the Australia Council, its board, committees and staff are affected.

speeches.speaker: Simon Crean
speeches.brief: Introduced the companion Consequential and Transitional Provisions Bill, which will repeal the nearly 40-year-old Australia Council Act 1975 and take effect from 1 July 2013, ensuring continuity for Council staff and its chair and deputy chair during the transition to a new skills-based board.

speeches.speaker: Judi Moylan
speeches.brief: Raised concerns that the Australia Council Bill 2013 removed community participation, freedom of expression, Australian identity, and Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander culture from the council's functions, arguing that arts funding should remain independent from executive government and support broader cultural benefits.

speeches.speaker: Michael Danby
speeches.brief: Summed up debate on the Australia Council Bill 2013, the most significant reform of the Australia Council's legislation in nearly 40 years, citing an additional $75.3 million invested over four years bringing total funding to over $200 million a year, and detailed amendments explicitly recognising Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander arts practice, freedom of expression in the arts, and peer assessment on funding committees.

speeches.speaker: Anthony Albanese
speeches.brief: Moved a procedural motion affirming the House's actions on the Australia Council Bill 2013 and its consequential bill, noting Senate committee concerns had been addressed, and thanked the opposition for supporting the housekeeping motion to transmit the bills to the Senate.

speeches.speaker: Gary Humphries
speeches.brief: Senator Brandis and the speaker were accused by Senator Milne of neglecting their duty in drafting amendments to the Australia Council Bill, but the speaker argued the amendments properly included references to freedom of speech and arts practice, promotion, understanding and enjoyment.
